But he, beckoning unto them with the hand to hold their peace, declared unto them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. And he said, Go shew these things unto James, and to the brethren. And he departed, and went into another place.
A James later leads the church in Jerusalem (Acts 12:17; 15:13; 21:18), and Paul speaks of “James the Lord's brother” (Galatians 1:19). Whether that James is this apostle is disputed; see below.

VIEWS, WITH WHO HOLDS THEM · THIS PAGE
Is James son of Alphaeus the same man as “James the Lord's brother”? (In the order the views arose.)

Helvidius (about AD 380), who took the Lord's brothers as later sons of Joseph and Mary; the older view, first found in the apocryphal Gospel of James (its stories go back to the 2nd century), that they were Joseph's sons by an earlier marriage; A. C. McGiffert (1890); Philip Schaff (1890)
John says the Lord's brothers did not believe in him after the Twelve had been chosen, and Acts names the apostles and then, separately, “his brethren”.
Scholars John 7:5·Acts 1:13–14 A. C. McGiffert, 1890·Philip Schaff, 1890·Alexander Walker (trans.), 1886

Paul counts “James the Lord's brother” among the apostles he saw, and there were only two apostles named James; so Jerome took the Lord's brothers to be cousins, sons of the Mary who was the wife of Clopas.
Early church Galatians 1:19·John 19:25 Jerome (trans. W. H. Fremantle, 1893·M. G. Easton, 1897
